title: What to expect: CT scan

slides.title: How your visit goes.
steps: Change if needed. For some belly scans, you drink a contrast liquid first.
Lie on a table that slides through a ring, open on both ends. You may hold your breath briefly.
Get right back to your day. Results go to your doctor within 48 to 72 hours.

slides.title: Feeling warm is normal.
items: A small IV goes in your arm: just a quick pinch.
A warm flush or metal taste lasts only seconds.
An urge to pee is common, and it passes.
slides.footnote: Many CT scans need no contrast at all. Sources: NIH MedlinePlus; RadiologyInfo.org (ACR, RSNA).

slides.title: Before your CT scan
items: Contrast scan? You may skip food for a few hours. We'll tell you.
Had a reaction to contrast or iodine before? Tell us.
Tell us about kidney problems, diabetes or metformin.
Pregnant, or might be? Tell us first.
slides.footnote: Leave jewelry at home. Source: NIH MedlinePlus.

slides.title: Simple to book in Seminole.
cards: self-pay CT with and without contrast
slides.footnote: Radiologist reading included. With insurance, a doctor's order is needed. We check your benefits before your visit.

captions.gbp:
Have a CT scan coming up? Here's what to expect at Advanced Medical Imaging in Seminole. You lie on a table that slides through a ring that is open on both ends, and the scan itself usually takes just a few minutes. You may be asked to hold your breath for a few seconds. If your scan uses IV contrast, a warm feeling, a metallic taste or feeling like you need to urinate is normal and passes quickly; drink extra water afterward. Many CT scans need no contrast at all. Before your scan, tell us about any past reaction to contrast, kidney problems, diabetes or metformin, or if you are or might be pregnant. Afterward you can get right back to your day, and results go to your doctor within 48 to 72 hours. Self-pay CT is $295 without contrast and $395 with and without contrast, with no referral needed.

Book online at advancedimg.com. General information, not medical advice.

carousel: A technologist beside a CT scanner while a colleague reviews scan images. Open on both ends. Done in minutes.

How your visit goes: check in and change if needed, with a contrast drink first for some belly scans; lie on a table that slides through a ring open on both ends, and you may hold your breath briefly; get back to your day, with results to your doctor within 48 to 72 hours.
If your scan uses contrast, feeling warm is normal: a small IV in your arm, a warm flush or metal taste that lasts only seconds, a common urge to pee that passes, and drink extra water afterward.

Before your CT scan: for a contrast scan you may skip food for a few hours; tell us about a past reaction to contrast or iodine; tell us about kidney problems, diabetes or metformin; tell us if you are or might be pregnant.
Simple to book in Seminole: $295 self-pay CT without contrast, $395 with and without contrast, no referral needed for self-pay, same day often possible for self-pay.
